creative.body:
I started keeping a constipation calendar 11 months into Wegovy. One green check for the days I went. A red X for the days I didn't. By month 6 the page was almost all red. My husband saw it on the fridge last week and started crying.

I have a paper planner I bought at Target 3 years ago. It used to be for grocery lists and grandkids' birthdays and the dates my husband's medication needed refills.

Last June, on a Tuesday morning at 6:47am, I sat down at the kitchen table with a green pen and a red pen and I started a different kind of calendar.

A constipation calendar.

I am 56. I had been on Wegovy 11 months. Down 47 pounds. The most weight I had ever lost in my life. My knees stopped hurting. My A1C dropped almost a full point. People at church started asking me what I was doing.

And I had stopped going to the bathroom on my own.

The calendar started because I needed proof for my GI. Every time I went in she would ask, "How often are you going?" and I would say, "Not enough," and she would write something on the chart I could not read. I wanted numbers she could not argue with.

Green check. Red X. The fridge.

Month 1.

9 green. 21 red.

I brought the page to my appointment in a manila folder so it would not crease. I slid it across the desk to her. She picked it up, looked at the front of it for 4 seconds, and set it back down. She said, "Increase the Miralax to 3 times a day. Add Colace at night." She did not ask me what I was eating. She did not ask me if anything else had changed. The next patient was already on her screen. I sat in my car in the parking lot for 20 minutes after, holding the page on my lap, and I did not cry yet. I still thought month 2 would be better.

Month 2.

7 green. 23 red.

I brought the page back. She did not look at it this time. "Try a different fiber. Acacia powder. Sometimes the body needs a change." I told her I had been on 4 different fibers in a year. She said, "Stay on top of the Miralax. It's perfectly safe long term." I did not say anything. I put the page back in the folder.

Month 3.

6 green.

Same answer. Stronger laxative if needed. She wrote me a script for prescription Linzess and told me to give it 6 weeks. I filled it the same afternoon.

Month 4.

5 green.

The Sunday suppository was the only consistent green. Every Monday I had to be a functional person at my granddaughter's school drop-off and I had learned that the only way that happened was if I dosed myself Sunday afternoon and waited. The other 4 green checks that month were enemas. I started timing them around when my husband would not be home.

Month 5.

4 green. All of them enemas.

I stopped trying to predict my own body. I stopped accepting dinner invitations. I told my daughter I could not fly out for spring break.

Month 6.

3 green.

The page on the fridge looked like a bloodbath. I left it up because I was past hiding it. I had stopped feeling like a person who could be embarrassed.

The Friday morning Bill cried, he came in for his coffee at 6:50am like he always does. He stopped in front of the fridge. He stood there for what I think was a full minute, holding his empty mug. I watched him from the kitchen table. His shoulders started shaking before any sound came out. He set the mug on the counter so he would not drop it. He did not turn around. He said, "Honey. I did not know it had gotten this bad." Then he walked out of the kitchen and down the basement stairs and shut the door to his office.

Bill is 63. He retired 2 years ago after 38 years as an insurance adjuster. He is not a man who Googles symptoms. He is the man who fixes the gutters and watches Premier League. The Friday morning he cried at the fridge, he did not come up for lunch. He came up for dinner, ate maybe 6 bites of chicken, kissed me on the top of the head, and went back down. I heard him through the floorboards at 2am. I heard him again at 4am. He stayed down there all of Saturday too. Did not turn the TV on once. Reddit. The GLP-1 forums. PubMed abstracts he had to read 3 times to understand. He took notes the way he used to take notes on a contested claim, in the small spiral notebook he kept in his shirt pocket for 38 years. He told me later he filled 14 pages. I went to bed Saturday night and cried into the pillow because I thought I had finally broken him. I thought my body had cost us our marriage.

Sunday morning at 7:30am he came up the stairs with 2 mugs.

He set one in front of me at the kitchen table. He sat across from me. He looked tired in a way I had not seen since the year his father died.

He said, "I think I figured it out."

I waited.

He said, "The medication works in 2 places. Not 1."

I said, "What do you mean 2 places."

He said, "The appetite suppression happens in your brain. That is the engine of your weight loss. The 47 pounds. We do not want to undo that part."

I said, "And the second place."

He said, "Your stomach. The medication takes it from normal to nearly frozen. Food that should leave in 4 hours sits there for 10 or 12. While it sits, bacteria ferment it. Every red X on our fridge is happening up here." He pointed at his own ribs.

I said, "Not the colon."

He said, "Not the colon, honey. Miralax pulls water into the colon. Magnesium pulls water into the colon. Suppositories trigger the colon. Enemas physically flush the colon. Every product on the counter has been working 6 feet downstream from the actual problem. There is nothing in your colon to flush."

I said, "Then what works."

He said, "A plant compound called apigenin. Concentrated in celery. It works on the smooth muscle of the stomach wall. Not a laxative. Not a stimulant. Does not touch the brain part of the medication. The drug keeps doing its job. The food just stops rotting inside you."

I said, "Why has nobody told me this."

He said, "Because every doctor you have seen is treating the colon. They are scoping the wrong organ."

He held my hand across the table.

He said, "I am scared, honey. I read about women who have been on this protocol 5 and 6 years. Their bowels physically cannot move without a daily laxative anymore. We are 4 or 5 months from the wrong side of it."

I sat with that.

I want you to sit with it too.

Every red X on my calendar was not bad luck. It was not bad fiber choice. It was not me failing to drink enough water. It was the protocol my doctor had handed me, applied to the wrong organ, for 11 months. Every escalation she added was another product working downstream from the actual clog. The food was upstream. It had always been upstream. She had been flushing an empty pipe while my stomach sat frozen above it. And every month she pushed me deeper into laxative dependency, my own body forgot a little more how to move on its own. The calendar was not a record of my body failing. It was a record of a wrong protocol slowly disabling the body underneath it. Bill told me later that the part that scared him in the basement was reading the message-board accounts of women 5 and 6 years in. Some of them had stopped going on their own entirely. Their bowels had quit. He said he read 3 of those threads before he had to close the laptop and go upstairs and sit in the dark for 20 minutes before he could keep reading.

Bill said apigenin alone was not enough. The formulations that worked in the accounts he read had 2 other ingredients. Chlorophyllin, to bind the sulfur compounds the bacteria produce in the stalled stomach. A small targeted dose of soluble prebiotic fiber, not bulk-forming, not Metamucil, a different category entirely, to support the lower gut once the stomach started moving again. The brand that kept showing up was a small company called Motilli. Standardized apigenin extract from celery, not the cheap powder. He had ordered it Saturday night before he came to bed. Heart-shaped gummies. 2 a day. They would be at our door Wednesday.

I kept the calendar going.

Week 1 on Motilli. 1 green. The first 4 days were red and I told Bill at Wednesday dinner I did not think it was working. He said, give it time.

Week 2. 3 green. The first one was a Saturday morning and I sat on the edge of the tub afterward and could not remember the last time my body had done that without me forcing it. Bill came and sat on the bathroom floor next to me. We both cried.

Week 3. 5 green. My granddaughter was over on a Saturday and we made cookies and I ate 2 and laughed at a movie at 8pm.

Week 4. 6 green. I took the Miralax, the magnesium, the suppositories, and the unused enema off my counter and put them in a trash bag. Bill took the trash bag out before I could change my mind.

Week 6. 7 green out of 7. Bill saw the calendar that Sunday morning and said, "Took you long enough."

I am still keeping the calendar. 11 weeks straight of all green. I am down 53 pounds, still on Wegovy.

The June page is still on the fridge. Bill and I leave it there because we do not ever want to forget. Next to it I taped a picture I took the morning Bill carried the trash bag out, of the empty cabinet where the laxatives used to be. The 2 pages live next to each other now. Red and empty. Empty and clean.

The medication works in 2 places.

Brain part is the engine. Do not undo it.

Stomach part is where every red X is coming from.

Every product on every shelf works 6 feet downstream.

Apigenin works on the right organ.

I am not affiliated with the company. Motilli runs a 90-day money-back guarantee. They batch-produce because apigenin degrades from light and heat, so the bottles sell out for stretches. If you have a vacation, a holiday, a wedding coming up, I would not wait until next week.

The link is below.

Janet

P.S. Bill is not on Wegovy. He has no skin in this except mine. He spent 2 nights of his retirement reading about a medication he has never taken because he refuses to let me become someone the protocol broke. If your husband has walked past your fridge and not said anything yet, please give him this. Sometimes the rescue is the man who finally sits down and reads.
creative.title: My constipation calendar said 22 red X's last month. I'm 11 months into Wegovy.
